ShortDef: The .NET runtime that runs your compiled code: memory management, type safety and just-in-time compilation.
Details: C# compiles to intermediate language (IL). The CLR's JIT turns IL into machine code as the program runs, and its garbage collector frees memory you no longer use.
WhenToUse: Understanding startup time, memory use and why the same assembly runs on Windows, Linux and macOS.

ShortDef: Turning intermediate language into machine code while the program runs; Native AOT does it ahead of time instead.
Details: JIT gives fast steady-state speed after warm-up. Native AOT produces a self-contained native executable with fast startup and small memory use, at the cost of some reflection-heavy features.
WhenToUse: Choosing between normal publish and Native AOT for containers, serverless and command-line tools.

ShortDef: Automatic memory cleanup: the runtime finds objects nothing refers to and frees them.
Details: The GC is generational: short-lived objects are collected cheaply. Allocating less (pooling, Span<T>, avoiding needless strings) is the main way to reduce GC pauses.
WhenToUse: Diagnosing high memory use or latency spikes.

ShortDef: The package manager for .NET: libraries are downloaded from nuget.org into your project.
Details: Packages are referenced in the project file with exact versions. Central package management keeps versions consistent across many projects.
WhenToUse: Adding any third-party library, or publishing your own.

ShortDef: Giving a class the things it needs through its constructor instead of letting it create them.
Details: ASP.NET Core has a built-in container: you register services with a lifetime (singleton, scoped, transient) and the framework supplies them. It makes code testable and swappable.
WhenToUse: Almost every ASP.NET Core application; it is how the framework itself is composed.

ShortDef: A chain of small components that each handle part of an HTTP request, in order.
Details: Authentication, routing, CORS, compression and error handling are all middleware. Order matters: a component can short-circuit the rest.
WhenToUse: Cross-cutting behaviour such as logging, headers or rate limiting.

ShortDef: A concise way to define HTTP endpoints in ASP.NET Core with lambdas instead of controller classes.
Details: `app.MapGet("/items", () => ...)` is a complete endpoint. Route groups, filters and typed results keep larger APIs organised.
WhenToUse: Small services, microservices and APIs that do not need MVC conventions.

ShortDef: Build interactive web UI in C# and Razor instead of JavaScript.
Details: Blazor Server runs components on the server and updates the browser over a live connection; WebAssembly runs them in the browser. .NET 8 can mix both per component.
WhenToUse: Teams that want one language across server and UI.

ShortDef: A library for real-time communication between server and clients, using WebSockets when available.
Details: Hubs let the server push messages to connected clients. Blazor Server uses it under the hood for UI updates.

ShortDef: An object-relational mapper: work with database rows as C# objects and write queries in LINQ.
Details: A DbContext tracks changes and saves them in one unit. Migrations evolve the schema. Watch for N+1 queries and over-fetching; use `AsNoTracking` for read-only queries.
WhenToUse: Most line-of-business apps that use a relational database.

ShortDef: Versioned scripts that change a database schema in step with your code.
Details: `dotnet ef migrations add` compares your model to the last snapshot and writes the change. Apply them at deploy time, and review the SQL for destructive changes.
WhenToUse: Any time the shape of your data changes.

ShortDef: Query collections, XML or databases with the same readable C# syntax.
Details: `Where`, `Select`, `GroupBy` and friends describe what you want. With EF Core the expression becomes SQL; with in-memory lists it runs in your process. Deferred execution means a query runs when enumerated.
WhenToUse: Filtering, projecting and aggregating data anywhere in C#.

ShortDef: Write code that waits for slow work (network, disk, database) without blocking a thread.
Details: An `async` method returns a `Task`; `await` hands the thread back until the work finishes. In web servers this lets a few threads serve many requests. Avoid `.Result` and `.Wait()`, which can deadlock.
WhenToUse: Every I/O call in server code.

ShortDef: A view over a stretch of memory (array, string, stack) that avoids copying and allocating.
Details: A ref struct that lives on the stack. Slicing a Span creates no new array. Used heavily in parsing and high-throughput code.

ShortDef: Concise immutable data types with value equality and non-destructive copying.
Details: `record Person(string Name, int Age);` gives equality by value, a readable `ToString` and `with` expressions to copy with changes. Good for DTOs and messages.
WhenToUse: Data carriers where identity does not matter.

ShortDef: Compiler warnings that tell you where a reference might be null, so NullReferenceException becomes a build-time problem.
Details: Enable `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`. Types without `?` promise to be non-null; the compiler flags risky dereferences.
WhenToUse: New projects, and gradually in old ones.
